transcript:
00:00 Morgan Lee: Okay hi everyone, Morgan from Redwood - thanks for taking the time. we wanted to run through a quick onramp playbook and understand what you need to get to a first-call sprint.
00:10 Alex Chen: Hey, thanks. quick background - we're FableWorks, we build tools for animation studios to auto-suggest scene descriptions and dialog. our early prototype uses in-house models but we want a managed inference path for scale.
00:25 Dana Ruiz: yeah, goal is to have a 4-week pilot where product can hit a prototype integrated into our editor. concerns: latency, cost, and, uh, intellectual property retention.
00:35 Priya Patel: great; that's exactly what the quickstart is for. Morgan gonna run through credits and hosting options, and I can dig into performance and infra.
00:44 Morgan Lee: quick note — we give free pilot credits for new accounts, usually 100k token-equivalent to get you to a working integration. TTFT, time-to-first-token, should be under a day if you're on self-serve with our hosted API; if you need VPC or Private we usually need a short security review.
00:58 Samir Patel: when you say hosted, is data retained? what's retention policy? we need ephemeral logs, nothing stored long-term.
01:08 Morgan Lee: good call. hosted can be configured with shorter retention windows; by default logs exist for x days but for an enterprise pilot we can set retention and we also have Dedicated and Private — Dedicated gives you reserved GPU pools and isolation at the compute layer; Private is a VPC or on-prem package where the control plane is customer-managed.
01:25 Rae: do you have SOC2? customer-managed KMS? audit logs?
01:31 Priya Patel: yes SOC2 Type II, we integrate with common KMS providers for key wrapping and offer HSM options for Private. audit logs are available per-token and per-route in the Console. I'll send the security pack link after the call — apologies if the name gets butchered in the transcript, red-wood security pack.
01:45 Alex Chen: okay. for perf, our ideal P95 for short prompts is 200-400ms. is that realistic on hosted?
01:53 Jordan Kim: depends on model and sequence length; for smaller models and short prompts hosted can reach sub-200ms in many regions. for larger, or high concurrency, Dedicated gets you consistent P95. also batching and KV-caching behaviors matter — if you're doing streaming, you may see different latency characteristics.
02:12 Dana Ruiz: we stream token by token for editor suggestions, so bursty low-latency matters. what's the impact on cost if we try to keep P95 low?
02:21 Priya Patel: there's a tradeoff — lower latency usually means less aggressive batching and higher cost. we can recommend batching thresholds and quant profiles per workload. Redwood Optimize will suggest configs once we see traces.
02:35 Samir Patel: what's the path to first token for us? we have a small dev team, we'd prefer self-serve.
02:41 Morgan Lee: self-serve hosted: sign up, apply credits, we give sandbox keys, you call the text/generate endpoints. typical TTFT: hours for a simple integration, a day for baked-in product flows. for Dedicated: ~2-3 weeks to provision reserved capacity depending on region and commit. Private/VPC on-prem usually 4+ weeks because of network and security work.
03:02 Alex Chen: are there constraints re model catalog? we run some in-house models we might want to host behind Redwood.
03:08 Jordan Kim: we have curated open models and support customer-provided models on Dedicated/Private — some work required for compatibility, quantization, and kernel selection. we can onboard a model as part of the pilot if you want to test your model or we can recommend off-the-shelf ones.
03:25 Dana Ruiz: cool. sample workload: 1-2 second prompts, avg 60 tokens, high QPS at peak during compiles. we care about token cost curves for our monthly forecast.
03:34 Priya Patel: understood; we'll run a quick cost vs latency estimate once we get sample traces. rough rule: smaller model + higher quantizing = lower cost but sometimes more latency variance. we'll propose a profile.
03:48 Rae: legal question: is there support for SAML SSO and granular RBAC?
03:54 Morgan Lee: yes SAML/SSO, SCIM provisioning, role-based access controls in Console, and you can restrict keys by route and model. we'll include the admin setup doc.
04:06 Alex Chen: any big red flags about going hosted first?
04:09 Priya Patel: hosted is fastest to prototype. the biggest blocker is if you require complete on-prem isolation or an air-gapped environment. another wrinkle is data residency — if EU-only residency is needed we have region-specific hosting and Private deployments.
04:25 Dana Ruiz: for the pilot we may start with hosted but want a path to Dedicated if we scale. is it easy to migrate?
04:31 Jordan Kim: yes, our deployment abstraction makes it straightforward to pin model versions and route traffic to Dedicated; billing and quotas adjust accordingly. we can do a canary cutover.
04:41 Samir Patel: about troubleshooting — if we hit weird outputs or regressions, do you provide eval tooling or rollbacks?
04:48 Priya Patel: Redwood Console has evals and regression alerts tied to prompt sets, and rollouts support canary/A-B and automatic fallback to compatible variants.
04:58 Alex Chen: good. what's the smallest committed size for Dedicated?
05:02 Morgan Lee: for Dedicated it's a monthly commit — numbers depend on instance types; we'll include a few sizing options in pricing doc. many teams start with a smaller pool plus burst capacity.
05:12 Dana Ruiz: can we run a mini-benchmark with our prompts? we'd like to see P95 numbers and token cost per 1k requests.
05:18 Priya Patel: absolutely — plan: you share 2 workload traces and we'll run a focused benchmark. I can run it in our sandbox and share a spreadsheet with latency and cost breakdown.
05:27 Samir Patel: timeline — we'd like prototype in 4 weeks and decision to either go Dedicated or stay Hosted after that.
05:33 Morgan Lee: sounds reasonable. next steps: I'll send pricing and legal one-pager; Priya will create sandbox + keys and prepare sample prompt set; Jordan will prep a 5-min demo of streaming + embeddings.
05:45 Rae: one more security thing — do you support customer-managed KMS in Hosted?
05:49 Priya Patel: hosted supports customer KMS via envelope encryption for stored artifacts; Private lets you keep keys fully in your control. we'll detail that in the security pack.
05:59 Alex Chen: are there any gotchas around tokenization differences or prompt engineering when switching models?
06:05 Jordan Kim: tokenization can vary; we'll surface token counts in the Console and help with prompt templates. part of the pilot is to confirm parity and quality for your prompt sets.
06:18 Dana Ruiz: okay let's do it. send the links and we'll pick slot for benchmark next week.
06:23 Morgan Lee: perfect — we'll send items by end of day tomorrow. thanks everyone.
06:29 Samir Patel: thanks all.
06:32 (end)
